feature1.prompt: Email messages crash on non-ASCII domain when email encoding is non-unicode. When the computer hostname is set in a non-iso-8859-1 value (for example, '正宗'), the system encounters errors during the conversion of email header fields such as Message-ID. The crash occurs because the domain name is not converted to its ASCII-compatible (punycode) representation, leading to UnicodeEncodeError messages like those from the ascii or latin-1 codecs. The fix requires that the email components reliably convert non-ASCII domain names to punycode before embedding them in the headers, ensuring proper behavior even when the encoding is non-unicode.
feature1.hint_texts: This feature involves refactoring the code by creating a utility function that converts a domain name to punycode and integrating this function into the email processing modules. It includes adding the punycode function in django/utils/encoding.py and modifying key parts of the email processing such as domain conversion in django/core/mail/message.py, adjusting the retrieval of the FQDN in django/core/mail/utils.py, and updating similar logic in django/core/validators.py and django/utils/html.py. The goal is to consistently handle domain name conversion across the codebase to prevent encoding errors.
feature1.entrypoint:
Files to modify include:
- django/utils/encoding.py: Add the punycode(domain) function.
- django/core/mail/message.py: Update the domain handling in functions like sanitize_address and in the message() method to use punycode.
- django/core/mail/utils.py: Change get_fqdn() to incorporate punycode conversion when retrieving the hostname.
- django/core/validators.py: Replace manual idna encoding with a call to punycode for URL validation.
- django/utils/html.py: Refactor the netloc conversion logic to use punycode instead of manual idna encoding.

feature2.prompt: Email messages crash on non-ASCII domain when email encoding is non-unicode. When the computer hostname is configured with non-iso-8859-1 characters (for instance, '正宗' or similar unicode values), the email system attempts to encode header fields like Message-ID without converting the domain name to punycode. This omission triggers UnicodeEncodeError exceptions due to the inability of encodings like iso-8859-1 to represent non-ASCII characters. The solution requires that the system converts non-ASCII domain names to their punycode representation before inclusion in email headers, ensuring that emails are processed without error.
feature2.hint_texts: This feature focuses on adding a dedicated test case that simulates an environment with a non-ASCII hostname and verifies that email headers are correctly converted to include a punycode domain. Developers should implement a test that patches the DNS or hostname values to a unicode string and confirms that the Message-ID header includes the punycode representation (for example, '@xn--p8s937b>'). The test should demonstrate a failure when the fix is not applied and then a successful pass once the domain conversion is correctly integrated.
feature2.entrypoint: File to modify: tests/mail/tests.py. In this file, add a new test case that patches the DNS name (or hostname) to a unicode value and sends an email with 'iso-8859-1' encoding. The test should then check the Message-ID header to confirm that the domain is converted to punycode. Use the provided pattern for patching and validation as a guide.

collaboration_points.shared_resources: Both features interact with shared modules such as django/utils/encoding.py, django/core/mail/message.py, django/core/mail/utils.py, django/core/validators.py, and django/utils/html.py. The punycode function and its application serve as a common resource across the email processing code.
collaboration_points.integration_strategy: Feature 1 establishes the core functionality by refactoring the code to include the punycode conversion, while Feature 2 validates that these changes work as expected under the conditions that previously caused failures. Developers should integrate these changes by running the full test suite to ensure that existing functionality is preserved and that the new test case passes once the refactoring is complete.
collaboration_points.communication_needs: Teams working on Feature 1 and Feature 2 should coordinate on the behavior of the punycode conversion logic and agree on the expected output in email headers. Regular discussions and code reviews are recommended to ensure that both the refactoring and the new test case are fully aligned and that integration testing is smooth.
